name: Trapped longs: weekly drop while longs still pay positive funding, short continuation
rule: Conventions: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k), latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null -> treat bar as missing). fdm(n,k)=mean of fd(j) for j=k-n+1..k skipping nulls, undefined unless >=n/2 non-null; any undefined input -> return 0. holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=5. r5=close[i]/close[i-5]-1. m=fdm(3,i). If r5<=-0.08 AND m>=0.0001 (longs still paying at least the 0.01%/8h baseline) -> -1 for 5 bars; else 0.
rationale: A sharp weekly drop with funding still positive means leveraged longs have not capitulated and face margin calls; forced selling should extend the move for several days.
source: Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov (2023) 'Crypto carry', BIS Working Paper 1087; Brunnermeier & Pedersen (2009) 'Market liquidity and funding liquidity', RFS

name: Trend long gated by funding crowding percentile (own 180-day history)
rule: Conventions: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k), latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null -> treat bar as missing). fdm(n,k)=mean of fd(j) for j=k-n+1..k skipping nulls, undefined unless >=n/2 non-null; any undefined input -> return 0. Signal mode. m(k)=fdm(14,k). Keep a ring of the last 180 defined m values (push once per bar). When ring is full, p = fraction of ring values strictly below m(i). Long (1) iff close[i]>sma(close,100) AND p<=0.75; else 0. Re-evaluated every bar. Clarification: push m(i) into the ring first, so the ring holds the 180 defined values ending at i inclusive; p is computed after the push; output 0 until the ring is full.
rationale: Uptrends carried with funding near the top of the coin's own range are crowded and fragile; staying long only when positioning is not at its own extreme tests whether crowding, not the trend, drives crashes.
source: Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov (2023) 'Crypto carry', BIS Working Paper 1087; Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012) 'Time series momentum', JFE

name: Funding acceleration exhaustion: fade a rally when funding jumps within a week
rule: Conventions: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k), latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null -> treat bar as missing). fdm(n,k)=mean of fd(j) for j=k-n+1..k skipping nulls, undefined unless >=n/2 non-null; any undefined input -> return 0. holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=5. m=fdm(3,i), mLag=fdm(3,i-7), r7=close[i]/close[i-7]-1. If m-mLag>=0.00015 AND r7>=0.10 -> -1 for 5 bars; else 0.
rationale: Funding that rises fast alongside a 10% weekly rally is the signature of leveraged chasing; the level of funding matters less than how quickly new longs arrived, and a fast build leaves the market fragile.
source: Brunnermeier & Pedersen (2009) 'Market liquidity and funding liquidity', RFS; Binance perpetual funding mechanism docs (premium index + clamp)

name: Unlevered rally: 10-day gain while funding fell, long continuation
rule: Conventions: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k), latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null -> treat bar as missing). fdm(n,k)=mean of fd(j) for j=k-n+1..k skipping nulls, undefined unless >=n/2 non-null; any undefined input -> return 0. holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, holdBars=10. r10=close[i]/close[i-10]-1. m=fdm(5,i), mPrev=fdm(5,i-10). If r10>=0.10 AND m<mPrev AND m<=0.0001 -> +1 for 10 bars; else 0.
rationale: A rally during which funding cools to baseline was financed by spot buyers rather than leverage, so there is less forced unwinding ahead than in a funding-fuelled rally.
source: Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov (2023) 'Crypto carry', BIS Working Paper 1087; Hong & Yogo (2012) JFE

name: Sustained 7-day funding extreme: fade crowded side in both directions
rule: Conventions: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k), latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null -> treat bar as missing). fdm(n,k)=mean of fd(j) for j=k-n+1..k skipping nulls, undefined unless >=n/2 non-null; any undefined input -> return 0. holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=7. m=fdm(7,i). If m>=0.0004 (about 44%/yr annualised) -> -1 for 7 bars. Else if m<=-0.0002 -> +1 for 7 bars. Else 0.
rationale: A week-long averaged funding extreme means one side has paid heavily to stay in; persistence over seven days is a stricter and different test than the single-print fade already in the registry.
source: Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov (2023) 'Crypto carry', BIS Working Paper 1087

name: Fear on the index but levered longs on the coin: short the disagreement
rule: Conventions: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k), latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null -> treat bar as missing). fdm(n,k)=mean of fd(j) for j=k-n+1..k skipping nulls, undefined unless >=n/2 non-null; any undefined input -> return 0. fng(k)=ctx.fearGreed(k), alternative.me Fear & Greed 0-100 for the day of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=7. If fng(i)<=30 AND fdm(3,i)>=0.0001 -> -1 for 7 bars; else 0.
rationale: When market sentiment is fearful yet perp traders on this coin still pay to be long, the survey and the positioning disagree; leveraged longs are the ones left to liquidate.
source: Baker & Wurgler (2006) 'Investor sentiment and the cross-section of stock returns', JF; Brunnermeier & Pedersen (2009) RFS

name: Greed on the index but unlevered coin: long the disagreement
rule: Conventions: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k), latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null -> treat bar as missing). fdm(n,k)=mean of fd(j) for j=k-n+1..k skipping nulls, undefined unless >=n/2 non-null; any undefined input -> return 0. fng(k)=ctx.fearGreed(k), alternative.me Fear & Greed 0-100 for the day of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, holdBars=10. If fng(i)>=70 AND fdm(3,i)<=0.00005 (below the 0.01% baseline) -> +1 for 10 bars; else 0.
rationale: Greed with no leverage on the coin means demand is spot-led, so the usual greed-then-crash path through liquidations is less likely.
source: Baker & Wurgler (2006) 'Investor sentiment and the cross-section of stock returns', JF; Schmeling et al. (2023)

name: Coin-denominated open-interest build in an uptrend
rule: oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k), USD notional open interest, latest hourly snapshot known at close of bar k (null -> return 0). Signal mode. coinOI(k)=oi(k)/close[k] (removes the price effect from USD open interest). g=coinOI(i)/coinOI(i-14)-1. State pos. Enter long when g>0.10 AND close[i]>sma(close,50). Exit to 0 when g<=0 OR close[i]<=sma(close,50). Otherwise keep pos. Clarification: if oi(i) or oi(i-14) is null return 0 (and drop to flat); pos persists across bars otherwise.
rationale: USD open interest rises mechanically with price; open interest in coin terms rises only when new contracts are opened, so a sustained build alongside an uptrend measures real participation.
source: Hong & Yogo (2012) 'What does futures market interest tell us about the macroeconomy and asset prices?', JFE; Bessembinder & Seguin (1993) 'Price volatility, trading volume and market depth', JFQA

name: New shorts opening into a 3-day drop: short continuation
rule: oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k), USD notional open interest, latest hourly snapshot known at close of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=4. r3=close[i]/close[i-3]-1, d=oi(i)/oi(i-3)-1. If r3<=-0.05 AND d>=0.05 -> -1 for 4 bars; else 0.
rationale: Price down while open interest rises means fresh shorts, not long liquidation, drove the move; this tests the continuation view against the squeeze-reversal view already in the registry.
source: Hong & Yogo (2012) 'What does futures market interest tell us about the macroeconomy and asset prices?', JFE; Bessembinder & Seguin (1993) JFQA

name: Open-interest stretch (60-day z>1.5) with price rolling over: short
rule: oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k), USD notional open interest, latest hourly snapshot known at close of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=7. Keep ctx.rolling(60) of oi(k) pushed once per bar. z=(oi(i)-mean)/std once full. If z>=1.5 AND close[i]<close[i-3] -> -1 for 7 bars; else 0. Clarification: if oi(i) is null do not push and return 0; z uses the 60 values ending at i inclusive (push first); population std; return 0 if std==0.
rationale: Open interest far above its recent norm is stored liquidation fuel; once price starts to roll over the stretched positions are the first to be forced out.
source: Brunnermeier & Pedersen (2009) 'Market liquidity and funding liquidity', RFS; Hong & Yogo (2012) JFE

name: Open-interest shock day: follow the day's direction for 3 days
rule: oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k), USD notional open interest, latest hourly snapshot known at close of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=3. d=oi(i)/oi(i-1)-1, r1=close[i]/close[i-1]-1. If d>=0.06 AND r1>=0.03 -> +1 for 3 bars; if d>=0.06 AND r1<=-0.03 -> -1 for 3 bars; else 0.
rationale: A day with a 6% jump in open interest and a 3% move is a position-initiating day; the daily-horizon version of the hourly impulse test checks whether such days continue over three sessions.
source: Bessembinder & Seguin (1993) JFQA; Binance futures open interest metrics

name: Crowding count: funding, open interest, sentiment all uncrowded
rule: Conventions: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k), latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null -> treat bar as missing). fdm(n,k)=mean of fd(j) for j=k-n+1..k skipping nulls, undefined unless >=n/2 non-null; any undefined input -> return 0. oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k), USD notional open interest, latest hourly snapshot known at close of bar k (null -> return 0). fng(k)=ctx.fearGreed(k), alternative.me Fear & Greed 0-100 for the day of bar k (null -> return 0). Signal mode. fm(k)=fdm(7,k); og(k)=oi(k)/oi(k-14)-1. Rings of the last 180 defined fm and og values (push once per bar). c1=1 if fm(i) is above the 80th percentile of its ring (ring full); c2=1 likewise for og(i); c3=1 if fng(i)>=70. crowd=c1+c2+c3. Long iff crowd==0 AND close[i]>sma(close,100); else 0. Clarification: push fm(i) and og(i) first (ring = 180 values ending at i inclusive; only when the value is defined). Return 0 until both rings are full and fng(i) is non-null. c1=1 iff the fraction of fm ring values strictly below fm(i) is >=0.80; c2 likewise for og.
rationale: Three independent crowding gauges (funding, new open interest, sentiment) combined test whether the whole positioning picture, rather than any single gauge, gates trend profits.
source: Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov (2023) 'Crypto carry', BIS Working Paper 1087; Baker & Wurgler (2006) 'Investor sentiment and the cross-section of stock returns', JF

name: Hourly EMA(24/120) trend confirmed by 24-bar mean funding
rule: Conventions: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k), latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null -> treat bar as missing). fdm(n,k)=mean of fd(j) for j=k-n+1..k skipping nulls, undefined unless >=n/2 non-null; any undefined input -> return 0. Signal mode, longShort. e1=ctx.ema('close',24,i), e2=ctx.ema('close',120,i), m=fdm(24,i) (mean of the last 24 hourly bar readings, about three settlements). If e1>e2 AND m>0 -> +1. If e1<e2 AND m<0 -> -1. Else 0. Re-evaluated every bar. Clarification: m is computed over the last 24 hourly bars with the skip-null convention above; return 0 if undefined.
rationale: Funding sign is a free vote on which side is paying for the trend; requiring trend and funding to agree tests the common retail rule 'trade with the funding-confirmed side'.
source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012) JFE; Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov (2023) 'Crypto carry', BIS Working Paper 1087

name: 24h long-liquidation bottom: price and open interest both drop, buy
rule: oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k), USD notional open interest, latest hourly snapshot known at close of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, holdBars=24. r=close[i]/close[i-24]-1, d=oi(i)/oi(i-24)-1. If r<=-0.04 AND d<=-0.05 -> +1 for 24 bars; else 0.
rationale: A 4% fall with 5% of open interest vanishing in a day is long liquidation; when the forced sellers are gone, the quadrant (price down, open interest down) is the classic bottoming pattern.
source: Hong & Yogo (2012) 'What does futures market interest tell us about the macroeconomy and asset prices?', JFE; Brunnermeier & Pedersen (2009) 'Market liquidity and funding liquidity', RFS

name: Hourly fade of an upmove carried by high funding
rule: Conventions: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k), latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null -> treat bar as missing). fdm(n,k)=mean of fd(j) for j=k-n+1..k skipping nulls, undefined unless >=n/2 non-null; any undefined input -> return 0. holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=12. m=fdm(24,i), r=close[i]/close[i-24]-1. If m>=0.0003 AND r>=0.04 -> -1 for 12 bars; else 0.
rationale: A 4% day-long rise while funding is three times baseline is a leverage-fuelled move; the hourly horizon tests whether the unwind arrives within hours rather than days.
source: Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov (2023) 'Crypto carry', BIS Working Paper 1087; Brunnermeier & Pedersen (2009) 'Market liquidity and funding liquidity', RFS

name: RSI(3) oversold dip bought only in fear
rule: fng(k)=ctx.fearGreed(k), alternative.me Fear & Greed 0-100 for the day of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, holdBars=3. If ctx.rsi(3,i)<=15 AND fng(i)<=35 -> +1 for 3 bars; else 0.
rationale: Short-term oversold bounces are the best documented crypto reversal; conditioning on market fear tests whether panic sentiment amplifies the snap-back.
source: Connors & Alvarez (2008) 'Short Term Trading Strategies That Work'; Baker & Wurgler (2006) 'Investor sentiment and the cross-section of stock returns', JF

name: RSI(3) overbought spike shorted only in greed
rule: fng(k)=ctx.fearGreed(k), alternative.me Fear & Greed 0-100 for the day of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=3. If ctx.rsi(3,i)>=90 AND fng(i)>=70 -> -1 for 3 bars; else 0.
rationale: Overbought extremes inside a greedy market are the mirror of the panic dip; the test asks whether euphoria produces a reliable three-day pullback.
source: Connors & Alvarez (2008); Baker & Wurgler (2006) 'Investor sentiment and the cross-section of stock returns', JF

name: Fear streak exhaustion: first neutral close after 7+ days of fear
rule: fng(k)=ctx.fearGreed(k), alternative.me Fear & Greed 0-100 for the day of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, holdBars=20. State s = consecutive bars ending at i-1 with fng<35. If fng(i)>=35 AND s>=7 -> +1 for 20 bars; else 0. s resets to 0 on any bar with fng>=35. Clarification: a null fng resets s to 0 and returns 0.
rationale: A long unbroken stretch of fear that finally ends marks selling exhaustion; waiting for the exit from fear avoids catching the knife during it.
source: Baker & Wurgler (2006) 'Investor sentiment and the cross-section of stock returns', JF; Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed methodology

name: Greed streak exhaustion: first non-greedy close after 7+ days of greed, short
rule: fng(k)=ctx.fearGreed(k), alternative.me Fear & Greed 0-100 for the day of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=10. State s = consecutive bars ending at i-1 with fng>=70. If fng(i)<70 AND s>=7 -> -1 for 10 bars; else 0. s resets on any bar with fng<70. Clarification: a null fng resets s to 0 and returns 0.
rationale: A week or more of greed ending is the point sentiment turns; this mirrors the fear-streak test and is run separately because greed and fear exits are not symmetric in crypto.
source: Baker & Wurgler (2006) 'Investor sentiment and the cross-section of stock returns', JF

name: Sentiment residual: Fear & Greed z-score minus 20-day return z-score
rule: fng(k)=ctx.fearGreed(k), alternative.me Fear & Greed 0-100 for the day of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=10. Keep two ctx.rolling(90): one of fng(k), one of r20(k)=close[k]/close[k-20]-1 (push once per bar when both defined). zF, zR = (latest - mean)/std once full. res=zF-zR. If res<=-1.5 (index more fearful than price implies) -> +1 for 10 bars; if res>=1.5 -> -1 for 10 bars; else 0. Clarification: push only on bars where fng(i) and r20(i) are both defined; z-scores use the 90 values ending at i inclusive (push first); population std; return 0 if either std==0 or ring not full.
rationale: The index mixes price momentum with other inputs; the part of sentiment not explained by recent price is a cleaner read of mood, and extremes of that residual may mean-revert.
source: Baker & Wurgler (2006) 'Investor sentiment and the cross-section of stock returns', JF; Brown & Cliff (2004) 'Investor sentiment and the near-term stock market', JEF

name: Rising sentiment inside an uptrend: 14-day Fear & Greed improvement
rule: fng(k)=ctx.fearGreed(k), alternative.me Fear & Greed 0-100 for the day of bar k (null -> return 0). Signal mode. State pos. d=fng(i)-fng(i-14). Enter long when d>=15 AND close[i]>sma(close,50). Exit to 0 when d<=0 OR close[i]<=sma(close,50). Otherwise keep pos. Clarification: if fng(i) or fng(i-14) is null return 0 and clear pos.
rationale: Sentiment that is improving fast while price is trending is a momentum-of-mood signal, distinct from buying a jump out of fear; it asks whether improving mood adds anything to trend following.
source: Baker & Wurgler (2006) 'Investor sentiment and the cross-section of stock returns', JF; Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012) JFE

name: Re-leveraging after fear: funding turns positive within 10 days of fear
rule: Conventions: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k), latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null -> treat bar as missing). fdm(n,k)=mean of fd(j) for j=k-n+1..k skipping nulls, undefined unless >=n/2 non-null; any undefined input -> return 0. fng(k)=ctx.fearGreed(k), alternative.me Fear & Greed 0-100 for the day of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, holdBars=20. f3=fdm(3,i), f3p=fdm(3,i-1). fearRecent = min of fng(j) for j=i-9..i <=30. If fearRecent AND f3>0.00005 AND f3p<=0.00005 -> +1 for 20 bars; else 0. Clarification: null fng values are skipped in the 10-day min; if all are null return 0.
rationale: After a fear episode the first return of leverage on the long side confirms risk appetite is back; entering on that cross trades confirmation rather than the bottom.
source: Baker & Wurgler (2006) 'Investor sentiment and the cross-section of stock returns', JF; Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov (2023) 'Crypto carry', BIS Working Paper 1087

name: Open interest shrinking while price breaks a 10-day high
rule: oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k), USD notional open interest, latest hourly snapshot known at close of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, holdBars=7. d=oi(i)/oi(i-10)-1. If d<=-0.05 AND close[i]>ctx.donchian(10,i-1).upper -> +1 for 7 bars; else 0.
rationale: A breakout on shrinking open interest is a short-covering break with little leverage above it; this tests the continuation view against the fade-short-covering view in the registry.
source: Hong & Yogo (2012) 'What does futures market interest tell us about the macroeconomy and asset prices?', JFE; Bessembinder & Seguin (1993) JFQA

name: Paid-to-hold trend: long while weekly funding is negative and price above 20-day mean
rule: Conventions: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k), latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null -> treat bar as missing). fdm(n,k)=mean of fd(j) for j=k-n+1..k skipping nulls, undefined unless >=n/2 non-null; any undefined input -> return 0. Signal mode. State pos. m=fdm(7,i). Enter long when m<0 AND close[i]>sma(close,20). Exit to 0 when m>=0.0001 OR close[i]<=sma(close,20). Otherwise keep pos.
rationale: Longs are paid funding while shorts pay, so negative-funding uptrends combine carry income with trend; the exit waits for funding to normalise.
source: Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov (2023) 'Crypto carry', BIS Working Paper 1087

name: Fear plus open-interest purge: buy
rule: oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k), USD notional open interest, latest hourly snapshot known at close of bar k (null -> return 0). fng(k)=ctx.fearGreed(k), alternative.me Fear & Greed 0-100 for the day of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, holdBars=10. If fng(i)<=30 AND oi(i)/oi(i-7)-1<=-0.10 -> +1 for 10 bars; else 0.
rationale: Fear with 10% of open interest gone in a week means leverage was flushed during the panic; the leverage-based capitulation signal complements the funding-based one already tested.
source: Baker & Wurgler (2006) 'Investor sentiment and the cross-section of stock returns', JF; Brunnermeier & Pedersen (2009) 'Market liquidity and funding liquidity', RFS

name: Greed plus open-interest exit: distribution short
rule: oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k), USD notional open interest, latest hourly snapshot known at close of bar k (null -> return 0). fng(k)=ctx.fearGreed(k), alternative.me Fear & Greed 0-100 for the day of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=7. If fng(i)>=65 AND oi(i)/oi(i-7)-1<=-0.05 -> -1 for 7 bars; else 0.
rationale: Greed while positions are being closed means informed traders are leaving as the crowd arrives; open interest falling into greed has historically preceded drawdowns in futures markets.
source: Hong & Yogo (2012) 'What does futures market interest tell us about the macroeconomy and asset prices?', JFE; Baker & Wurgler (2006) 'Investor sentiment and the cross-section of stock returns', JF

name: Funding-confirmed SMA(20/50) cross, long and short
rule: Conventions: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k), latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null -> treat bar as missing). fdm(n,k)=mean of fd(j) for j=k-n+1..k skipping nulls, undefined unless >=n/2 non-null; any undefined input -> return 0. Signal mode, longShort. m=fdm(30,i). If sma(close,20)>sma(close,50) AND m>0 -> +1. If sma(close,20)<sma(close,50) AND m<0 -> -1. Else 0. Re-evaluated every bar.
rationale: Trade the moving-average trend only when the 30-day carry sign agrees with it; disagreement (uptrend with negative funding) means the market is not paying for the trend, so stand aside.
source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012) JFE; Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov (2023) 'Crypto carry', BIS Working Paper 1087

name: Participation regime: coin-OI/return correlation gates 10-day momentum
rule: oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k), USD notional open interest, latest hourly snapshot known at close of bar k (null -> return 0). Signal mode. x(k)=close[k]/close[k-1]-1, y(k)=coinOI(k)/coinOI(k-1)-1 where coinOI=oi/close. Keep ctx.rolling windows (30) of x, y, x*y, x*x, y*y pushed once per bar; rho = Pearson correlation over the last 30 bars once full. Long (1) iff rho>=0.3 AND close[i]/close[i-10]-1>0; else 0. Clarification: push only on bars where oi(i), oi(i-1), close[i-1] are defined (else return 0); rho uses the 30 values ending at i inclusive; return 0 if either variance is 0 or the window is not full.
rationale: When coin open interest rises on up days and falls on down days, price is led by new positions and momentum should work; when the sign is negative, rallies are short covering and momentum should fail.
source: Hong & Yogo (2012) 'What does futures market interest tell us about the macroeconomy and asset prices?', JFE; Bessembinder & Seguin (1993) JFQA

name: Panic day: one-day Fear & Greed drop of 12+ points, buy
rule: fng(k)=ctx.fearGreed(k), alternative.me Fear & Greed 0-100 for the day of bar k (null -> return 0). holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, holdBars=5. If fng(i-1)-fng(i)>=12 -> +1 for 5 bars; else 0.
rationale: A single-day collapse in the index marks a capitulation shock; the buy-the-panic rule is common folklore and cheap to test directly.
source: Baker & Wurgler (2006) 'Investor sentiment and the cross-section of stock returns', JF; Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed methodology

name: Hourly oversold bounce when funding is non-positive
rule: Conventions: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k), latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null -> treat bar as missing). fdm(n,k)=mean of fd(j) for j=k-n+1..k skipping nulls, undefined unless >=n/2 non-null; any undefined input -> return 0. holdBars=N means: after entry hold exactly N bars, no re-entry while held, then re-evaluate. Signal mode, holdBars=6. If fdm(24,i)<=0 AND ctx.rsi(14,i)<=25 -> +1 for 6 bars; else 0.
rationale: RSI oversold with non-positive funding means shorts, not longs, hold the leveraged side, so the bounce is less likely to be sold into by trapped longs.
source: Wilder (1978) 'New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems'; Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov (2023) 'Crypto carry', BIS Working Paper 1087
